chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Why Cab hated trash on stage and Milt's missed solo
summary: Cab hated paper on stage, and Milt explains his bowed solo Girl of My Dreams and how Cab blamed Dizzy for a spitball that landed beside them.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: And he'd make these spitballs. We didn't mind, see. And nobody minded. But the thing was with Cab, he liked a perfect stage. He didn't like to see no paper because he's a dancer, and if you have a gum wrapper or if you have a piece of gum, a rubber band or a label... People would take...they're sitting in the theatre, and they'd get

these chocolate bars. And they'd take the labels and crush them and throw them on the stage. Sometimes there would be a whole lot of trash on the stage. And Cab would be dancing, and he'd kick all that in the footlights...
So he'd have a clean stage.

Because a dancer can slip on it. He's conscious of it. So he comes ou and he'd see all these little-bitty things on it. "What is all this?" And he'd do it three or four times, and kick them off the stage. He was saying, "What's that? What's all that trash out there?" "Somebody's throwing spitballs." Well, somebody in the band, or Dizzy's throwin' it... And then he's watching for it. So he's in the wings, so he's watching...

Well, what really happened on that particular day was, I was playing this solo, "Girl Of My Dreams," which he had taught me, bowing like Slam Stewart. And I couldn't hear him them flatted fifths too cool. You know, when I got to the end ...[SINGS]..., I missed it a mile. And when I made it, any time I'd make it, did it all right, I'd look back at Diz. If I made it, Diz would say, "Great. You did it great" -- you know. And that day, it was a matinee performance, I missed that thing a mile. And I looked back at Dizzy, and Dizzy said, "You stink." And just as he did that, a spitball come up and it landed right out in the
spotlight, right beside us. Well, Cab was in the wings, and he looked when he saw the spitball... And he looked and he saw Diz do this -- and supposed it was Dizzy.

And when we come off... Everybody got off the stage at the end of the show, but I had to put my bass back up on the bandstand. So I'm standing there, and he stopped Dizzy, and he said, "Look, you little so-and-so, you, there's people out there entertaining the public and you're back there acting like a schoolkid throwing spitballs." And Dizzy said, "Fess, I didn't do it" -- we called him Fess. "Hey, Fess, I didn't do that." And then Cab started berating him, called it a bunch of lies to him -- and he had a couple off nice ladies standing off on the side waiting to see him anyway...
